Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Karen Rivera (Lumina VP Procurement), Dr. Alan Chu (Lumina CTO), Priya Nair (Lumina Security Engineer), Marcus Lee (Lumina Legal), Evan Park (Lumina Platform Lead)

Pilot scope, benchmarks and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have the procurement and security folks on the line so we'll focus the call on the redline, SLAs, and the pilot timeline.
[00:12] Karen Rivera: Yep thanks Sofia, we have about 45 minutes set aside, Marcus and I will be driving the legal review. quick ask up front - can you confirm data residency? we need EU data to stay in EU for certain workloads.
[00:22] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely, for hosted we have region pinning and for private deployments we can support customer VPC and on-prem. we'll call out that in the DPA, note that some telemetry for billing is retained in US but payloads can be restricted to eu-west-1.
[00:38] Marcus Lee: that's promising, but we want explicit clauses re: sub processors and certs, and we need KMS integration language - who holds keys?
[00:49] Daniel Cho: hi Marcus, Daniel from engineering - we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for private deployments and dedicated in VPC mode; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options. we can share architecture doc.
[01:05] Priya Nair: (security) also need SOC2 attestation, ISO certs, pen test reports; and does Redwood keep model outputs? what's retention?
[01:13] Maya Patel: quick note, we commonly offer configurable retention controls; default is 30 days for logs, customer data retention is configurable, and we can commit in the DPA.
[01:24] Dr. Alan Chu: on the tech side, we need SLA guarantees for latency at p95 under production load; our workflows are latency-sensitive for real-time triage, so dedicated capacity is of interest but pricing is a concern.
[01:39] Sofia Martinez: understood - our Dedicated offering has committed throughput + latency SLOs and an SLA backing uptime. for hosted we provide best-effort latency with region routing; if latency is critical you might want Reserved/Dedicated.
[01:53] Evan Park: whats the delta in cost between hosted and dedicated for the model sizes we discussed? we looked at your spreadsheet, but procurement needs ballpark for budgeting.
[02:03] Sofia Martinez: ballpark: hosted pay-as-you-go is typically 40-60% lower at low volume but at sustained throughput Dedicated with reserved nodes is more economical; i can send a pricing scenarios sheet.
[02:15] Karen Rivera: good, procurement needs the final price by next week to approve PO. can you commit to send final pricing and a sample SOW?
[02:24] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll send updated pricing + sample SOW by 2027-04-05 alongside the MSA redline.
[02:30] Marcus Lee: on the MSA redline, a couple of items: indemnity cap, data breach notification timelines, and audit rights. also want to see subprocessor list.
[02:42] Daniel Cho: for breach notification we typically commit to 72 hours for confirmed incidents and immediate notification for critical exfiltration. auditor access can be scoped - we can propose a SOC2 review window.
[02:55] Priya Nair: regarding KMS - if we hold keys, can Redwood still provide support without access to plaintext? we need remote debugging guarantees without key exposure.
[03:05] Daniel Cho: reasonable ask; we can set a support escalation flow that uses sessioned logs and structured telemetry, and for private deployments we can offer jumpbox-based assisted debugging with customer consent.
[03:20] Karen Rivera: timeline question - once MSA/DPA signed, how long to get pilot environment up? we want a 30-day pilot with throughput tests.
[03:29] Maya Patel: usually 2 weeks to provision a dedicated pilot environment once redlines and PO are done, then kick off the 30-day pilot. we will provide onboarding doc and dedicated CSM.
[03:40] Dr. Alan Chu: pilot success criteria - p95 latency < 400ms for 4k token requests, throughput of 50 requests/sec sustained, and quality regression < 2% vs our baseline.
[03:52] Daniel Cho: we'll take those numbers and build a benchmark plan; we have a pre-built script to simulate your traffic pattern. we'll share it after the call.
[04:02] Karen Rivera: procurement also wants to know cancellation terms and SLA credits.
[04:08] Sofia Martinez: cancellation terms are in the MSA; for Dedicated we have minimum term commitments but we can discuss flexible terms for pilot. SLA credits are standard - we'll include the explicit credit table in the redline.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: ok please make those tables explicit. also we need DPA language about deletion on termination and certification of deletion.
[04:30] Sofia Martinez: yes, we'll add deletion certification language and proof of deletion options.
[04:36] Evan Park: one more around integrations - we use Okta for SSO and HashiCorp Vault for secrets. can Redwood integrate?
[04:44] Daniel Cho: Okta SAML/SCIM supported for user SSO; Vault can be integrated for secrets via our KMS connectors on private deployments. for hosted we support BYOK flows to Vault-backed KMS with additional integration work.
[04:58] Priya Nair: good, please document the SCIM provisioning behavior.
[05:02] Sofia Martinez: will do, we'll add the SCIM/SSO integration doc link in the packet.
[05:05] Karen Rivera: any competitors references - we've had demos from CloudServeAI and Anthropic for similar features, what differentiates Redwood on the contract side?
[05:15] Sofia Martinez: typically our differentiators are production-first SLAs, flexible deployment modes (including private VPC), and explicit cost controls via batching/quantization recommendations; contract-wise we try to be pragmatic with enterprise redlines and a speedy onboarding motion.
[05:28] Marcus Lee: ok, last legal ask - can we get a list of third-party subprocessors and a dedicated contact for audits?
[05:36] Maya Patel: yes, we'll include a subprocessor list and provide a compliance contact.
[05:40] Dr. Alan Chu: on performance, Daniel, can you outline what we should expect in pilot vs prod? some variability is okay but p95 stability is key.
[05:50] Daniel Cho: in pilot we mirror production stacks but with scaled-down nodes; we can reserve capacity for the pilot so p95 should be representative. we'll instrument and provide token-level latency breakdowns.
[06:03] Karen Rivera: procurement item - if we sign an annual Dedicated commit, do we get discounted pricing for third-party services? we have other vendor discounts to coordinate.
[06:13] Sofia Martinez: we can include a negotiated discount schedule in the SOW for committed tiers and volume. we'll outline examples in the pricing scenarios.
[06:22] Evan Park: any legal hold concerns for research data? sometimes we need to freeze data sets.
[06:27] Marcus Lee: we'll include legal hold language in DPA if needed.
[06:30] Sofia Martinez: noted.
[06:33] (brief cross talk)
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: recap - actions: sending MSA/DPA redline, pricing scenarios, benchmark plan and onboarding checklist. target dates called out.
[06:47] Karen Rivera: thanks, please send all artifacts to procurement@luminahealth.com and cc alan and priya.
[06:54] Sofia Martinez: will do. any other final questions?
[06:58] Priya Nair: none from security, thanks.
[07:00] Sofia Martinez: great, we'll follow up. meeting adjourned.
